rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun most fully when it rises after sunset as a bright full moon, especially on nights fourteen to sixteen.
rows.anchor: Bu tam mânasıyla ayın on dördünden on altısına kadar “leyâl-i bîz” denilen bedir gecelerinde zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon can seem to follow the sun at other times, but before fullness it is incomplete and after the sixteenth night it increasingly lags behind sunset.
rows.anchor: On altısından sonra Şems’in gurûbundan gitgide teahhur ve tenâkusla uzaklaştığı için tâkip ve teba‘iyetten çıkmaya başladığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb talā derives from tulūw, meaning to follow behind; recitation is related because a reader follows and conveys words.
rows.anchor: “Tülüv” tâbi‘olmak, birine uyup ardınca gitmektir. Okumak mânasına “tilâvet” de bundandır.

rows.speaker: Atâ
rows.claim: Atā, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the moon remains risen when the sun sets, which occurs in the first half of the month.
rows.anchor: Bu İbn Abbas’tan Atâ’nın kavlidir.

rows.speaker: Katâde ile Kelbî
rows.claim: Qatada and Kalbi say the moon follows the sun by setting after it, as on the crescent night.
rows.anchor: Bu Katâde ile Kelbî’nin kavlidir.

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: Farra interprets following as the moon receiving its light from the sun.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ demiştir ki: Bu tülüvden murad Kamer’in Şems’ten ziyâ almasıdır

rows.speaker: Zeccâc
rows.claim: Zajjaj takes the phrase as the moon's turning and completion, when its light reaches fullness and it resembles the sun in illumination.
rows.anchor: Zeccâc demiştir ki: إِذَا تَلَىٰهَا istidâre ve kemâl zamanıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth possibility relates the moon's perceptible size and the world's benefits to its movement.
rows.anchor: bu âlemin mesâlihi, hareketine merbut olmakta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported senses share the idea of following or resembling the sun in rising, setting, light, size, or benefit; the moon also derives its light from the sun.
rows.anchor: Bu mefhum Kamer’in tehavvülâtında nûrunu Şems’ten ahzettiğini dahi dolayısıyla anlatmış olursa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crescent-night interpretation draws attention to the new moon, but restricting following to sunset alone lacks a decisive reason.
rows.anchor: İkinci vecih, ilk hilâle nazar-ı dikkati celbetmek itibariyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view illuminates the moon's day-by-day waxing toward fullness more broadly than the fourth view.
rows.anchor: Birinci vecih hilâlden tam bedre kadar nısf-ı evvelde yevmen fe-yevmen mütezâyid olan tekâmül safahâtını göstermek itibariyle dördüncüden daha şümullü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ultimately, the fourth view is clearest: the full moon resembles a secondary sun and its reflected light prepares for the soul's perfection.
rows.anchor: Fakat asıl maksud, Şems’in duhâsı gibi Kamer’in de o gāye-i kemâlde olan mehtâbına ve bunun ziyâ-yı Şems’e tâbi‘ve tâlî olduğunu anlatarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's reflected, nonfiery light leads from sensory evidence to intelligible truth, the seen to the unseen, and effect to its cause.
rows.anchor: mahz-ı nûr hâlinde akseden ve mahsüsten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading talā figuratively likens the moon's spreading the unseen sun's reflected light to a reciter explaining a Qur'anic verse; this evokes the purified soul and the Qur'an as light.
rows.anchor: bir kāriin Kitâbullah’tan bir âyet okuyarak mânasını delâlet-i lafziye ile anlatmasına benzetilecek olursa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajliyah means to make manifest, clarify, or polish; the pronoun refers to the sun, and the phrase describes clear daylight without cloud or haze.
rows.anchor: “Tecliye”, tecellî ettirmek; cilâ ve vuzuh vermek, yani iyice açıp izhar eylemektir. Zamir, zâhir olan Şems’e râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight is made the agent that unveils the sun even though it is the sun's own light reflected on earth, a noteworthy rhetorical reversal.
rows.anchor: yani Güneş’in eseri olan ziyânın Güneş’te müessir gösterilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unobstructed day makes light clearer, and clear light makes the sun more manifest; through light the sun is sensed, while clouds leave it known indirectly by reason.
rows.anchor: Gündüz hava bulutlu olunca Güneş doğrudan doğru görülmez, dolayısıyla ma‘kūl olarak bilinir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath draws attention to manifestation in the horizons and within the self, and to how an effect points to its effective cause.
rows.anchor: Bunda Güneş’in âfâk ve enfüste tecellîsi mâni‘bulunmamakla meşrut idiğine ve eserin lâzımı dahi zât-ı müessire delâlette âmil olduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath concerns night as it covers the sun and horizons, obscuring light in the onset or continuation of dense darkness.
rows.anchor: gecenin Güneş’i ve bütün âfâkı sarıp kaplayarak nûr ve ziyâyı tamamen örtmeye başladığı veya örtmekte istimrar üzere bulunduğu hâlindeki koyu karanlık hengâmına kasemdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with daylight reveals the importance of light and the value of inner awareness that feels its absence when outward light is gone.
rows.anchor: yine ziyânın ehemmiyetine ve bâhusus zâhirî nûr ve ziyânın gāib

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darkness alludes to the moon's obscuration and to the soul veiled from divine guidance by ignorance, disbelief, grief, heedlessness, inertia, or desire, as well as to death's moment.
rows.anchor: nefsin cehalet, küfür, gamm u kasvet, gaflet ü atâlet veya şehvet perdelerinin gaşeyânıyla Hak hidâyetinden mahrûmiyeti hâllerine ve fena lahzasına dahi işaret vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier oaths carry glad tidings, whereas this oath about darkness has a warning character.
rows.anchor: Onun için evvelki kasemler tebşîrî, bu kasem inzârî bir mâhiyeti hâizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from past forms for the preceding oaths to a present-future form here emphasizes darkness at its initial attack and while it persists.
rows.anchor: zulmetin ehemmiyeti ancak ilk hücum lahzasıyla istimrârı hengâmında olduğuna bir işarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oaths summarize the preceding surah: that surah moved from light to darkness and toward knowledge of God and self, ending with Thamud's ruin; this surah moves from annihilation toward witnessed light, purification, growth, and abiding in God.
rows.anchor: fenâdan nûr-ı şuhûda doğru tecellî, tezekkî ve nemâ ile bekā-billâha gidilecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous surah ended with a warning, while this one begins in warning and proceeds toward glad tidings; destruction of a people or world does not diminish the Creator, who can renew creation with day, male, and female.
rows.anchor: Bir kavmin ve hatta bütün âlemin helâk ve fenasıyla Hâlık’a bir eksiklik, bir ziyan gelmez, O’nun kudretine bir tevakkuf ârız olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night signifies cosmic and inward darkness; its definite article may refer to the whole kind of night or to a particular terrifying night, literally or figuratively.
rows.anchor: “leyl”in lâmı cinse masruf olarak gece cinsinin böyle bir lahzasına veya ahde mahmul olarak hakīkī ve mecâzî bütün mânasıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaghshā can mean that darkness covers the sun, daylight, all the horizons, grief, or the eyes, hearts, and faculties through sleep and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: karanlığıyla Güneş’i veya gündüzü veya örtebileceği her şeyi ile âfâkı ve hatta gam u kasveti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The encompassing night can carry a person from differentiation to unity, multiplicity to solitude, and witnessing to annihilation in an overwhelming immersion.
rows.anchor: insanı farktan cem‘e, kesretten halvete, şuhuddan fenâya götürmek üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the object of covering broadens the meaning and heightens terror; the wording also points back to the night covering the sun in the previous surah.
rows.anchor: Bununla evvelki sûredeki وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰهَا’ya [eş-Şems 91/4] işaret edilmiş olmakla beraber mef‘ûlün hazfinde daha ziyade bir ta‘mîm ve ibham ile tehvil vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional idhā asserts realization and, because the imperfect can indicate present or future, signals that the event may occur now or later.
rows.anchor: اِذَا tahakkuk ifade etmek ve muzâri‘hâl ve istikbâle muhtemil olmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image can warn of a town or people being engulfed by punishment, the era of ignorance around the Prophet's mission, death agonies, or resurrection events.
rows.anchor: bâhusus bi‘set-i seniyye sıralarında dünyayı sarmış bulunan devr-i cehalet hâline ve istikbâle ait olmak üzere de sekerât-ı mevt veya kıyamet ahvâline

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night here is the accidental darkness of passing-away after existence, not primordial nonexistence; at this moment the verses declare that all perishes except God's face, and readers pass from annihilation to abiding witness.
rows.anchor: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍۢ وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلَٰلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ [er-Rahmân 55/26-27] ve كُلُّ شَىْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُۥ [el-Kasas 28/88]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous surah swore by the day when it unveils the sun; here the oath is by the day in its own manifestation.
rows.anchor: Evvelki sûrede nehârın Şems’i tecliye ettiği vakte kasem edilmişti. Bunda ise nehârın kendi tecellîsine kasem edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifested day alludes to the manifestation of the sun of truth in unity and to the emergence of Islam.
rows.anchor: Bunda hak güneşinin vahdetle tecellîsine ve İslâm’ın zuhûruna işaret vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the pronouns grammatically refer to night and day, in reality both the covering and the manifestation belong to God.
rows.anchor: يَغْشٰى ve تَجَلَّىٰ zamirleri zâhiren biri “leyl”e biri “nehâr”a râci‘olmakla beraber, hakikatte ikisi de Hâlık teâlâ’ya râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human endeavors are scattered, inconsistent, and disordered, although well-being and success depend on unity, cooperation, and gathering together.
rows.anchor: mesâîniz birbirini tutmaz surette müteferrik, dağınık, nizamsızdır. Hâlbuki hayat ve felah nizâm-ı tevhid ile te‘âvün ve ictimâ‘a merbuttur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that people's efforts differ in moral quality and rank: some work well or highly, others badly or poorly, and some believe while others do not.
rows.anchor: Yahut sa‘yleriniz çok farklıdır. Kimi iyi çalışır kimi kötü, kimi yüksek kimi aşağı, kimi imanlı kimi imansız.

rows.speaker: مفسّرین
rows.claim: Exegetes explain shattā as efforts with differing outcomes: faith, obedience, and good deeds versus disbelief, disobedience, and sins.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn burada bunu hükümleri muhtelif, birbirinden uzak, kimi iman ve itaat ve hasenât gibi hayr u hidâyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can also be understood through the contrast of disagreement and agreement, as expressed in the cited statement about those shown mercy.
rows.anchor: mazmûnuna göre ihtilâf ve ittifak ile mülâhaza da mümkindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest purpose is to warn against fragmentation like that of the age of ignorance and to urge unity in thought and ordered action.
rows.anchor: asıl murad, câhiliyette olduğu gibi teşettüt ve tefrikanın kendisinden tahzir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fragmented effort is worse than idleness because its mutually cancelling work is futile toil and therefore an evil to avoid.
rows.anchor: say‘de teşettüt ve perişanlık yekdiğerini nâkız olmak itibariyle haddizâtında atâletten daha fena olan boşuna bir te‘ab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conflicting desires and goals disarray hearts through disbelief, idolatry, and sin; failure to affirm God's unity ruins both individuals and society.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın birliğine hakkıyla iman edememekten münba‘is olan bu hâl ise ferdin de cemiyetin de perişanlığıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruin of divided efforts is clarified by the image of an idolater falling from the sky and by disbelievers' deeds scattered like ashes in a storm.
rows.anchor: وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means paying wealth's due and spending for good, including freeing slaves, feeding the needy in hardship, and supporting Muslims against enemies.
rows.anchor: hayır necdine çıkan akabeyi iktiham etmek üzere fekk-i rakabe ve darlık günlerinde bîçârelere it‘âm ve müslimîni düşmanlara karşı müdafaa ve takviye eylemek gibi vücûh-i hayra sarf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa means fearing God, following obedience, and protecting oneself from evil and forbidden acts, as in the description of those who avoid major sins.
rows.anchor: Allah’tan korkup tâat yolunu tutarak kendini teşettütten, fenalıktan, menhiyyâttan sakınmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing in al-husnā means affirming real goodness, distinguishing virtue from vice, and trusting that good-doers receive better and greater reward, Paradise, and a beautiful final outcome.
rows.anchor: hakikatte bir güzellik ve güzellerin en güzeli bulunduğuna inanmış; iyiyi kötüyü, fazileti rezîleti fark etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husnā is the feminine form of the superlative ahsan, used as a noun after its qualified noun is omitted.
rows.anchor: “Hüsnâ” mâlum ki yukarılarda geçtiği üzere “ahsen” ism-i tafdîlinin müennesi, daha güzel veya en güzel mânasına sıfat olduğu hâlde, mevsûfunun hazfiyle isim olarak kullanılmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpretations of al-husnā include the best trait such as faith or ihsan, the best word such as tawhid or the Qur'an, the best religion of Islam, or the best recompense and Paradise.
rows.anchor: “haslet-i hüsnâ” en güzel haslet: iman ve ihsan hasleti veya “kelime-i hüsnâ” en güzel kelime: kelime-i tevhid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, al-husnā most usefully means the better reward and final outcome promised to those who do good, or the verses promising it.
rows.anchor: siyâka nazaran en zâhir ve en müfid olan mâna ihsan eden, Allah için güzellik yapan muhsinlere ileride daha güzeliyle karşılık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Practical affirmation matters: one who believes the promise tries sincerely to realize goodness, rather than merely saying the promise is true.
rows.anchor: mücerred doğrudur demek değil, fiilen sadakatle icrâsı dahi matlub

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in al-husnā precedes giving and taqwa in the order of being, but the text mentions those acts first for two rhetorical reasons.
rows.anchor: tertîb-i vücûdîde i‘tâ ve ittikāya mukaddemdir. O fazilet ve ihsan, o tasdîke terettüb eder. Böyle iken zikirde i‘tâ ve ittikānın takdim edilmesinde iki nükte vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reason is that affirmation is required in practice as well as belief and speech: giving and taqwa are primary acts, and verbal belief without them does not earn the promise of ease.
rows.anchor: fiiliyyâtta hiç eseri zâhir olmayan tasdîke burada zikrolunacak yüsrâ vaadi terettüb etmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer expects the afterlife to be better, remains optimistic about good and pessimistic about evil, and accepts hardship for virtue because it ends in happiness.
rows.anchor: sonu pek güzel saadet olduğuna, rezîletin önü rahat ve lezzet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ihsan gives delight, such a person gives gladly, does not begrudge wealth or effort spent on good, and endures sacrifice to avoid evil.
rows.anchor: i‘tâ ve ittikāyı huzur ve itmi’nân-ı kalb ile seve seve yapar, hayra sarfeylediği mal ve cehde acımaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second reason for mentioning giving and taqwa first is that effects and recompense follow their causes and deeds; al-husnā is their resulting goal.
rows.anchor: müsebbeb sebebden, ivaz mu‘avvazdan, ecr ü mükâfâta istihkak vazife ve amelden muahhar olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusrā is the easiest path to comfort and happiness, including easy reckoning and entry into Paradise.
rows.anchor: kolay hesab ile cennete girmek gibi refâh ü saadet yolu olan hayır yoluna hazırlayacağız

rows.speaker: مفسّرین
rows.claim: Exegetes explain taysīr as preparing and making ready, by analogy with fitting a horse with bridle and saddle for riding.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn demişlerdir ki işbu فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ’de teysir tehyi’e etmek, âmâde kılmak mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For one who trusts the promise, the good path that is difficult for others becomes easy to undertake joyfully, and good deeds multiply the means of reaching the goal.
rows.anchor: o o müşkilâtı kolaylıkla iktiham edecek, hayır amellere kolaylıkla muvaffak olup rahat ve saadete erecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds wealth and avoids paying what is due.
rows.anchor: Ve amma buhl etmiş malını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istighnā means imagining oneself already self-sufficient, free of future need and protection, and absorbed in one's present self, wealth, and worldly desires.
rows.anchor: kendini gınâya ermiş, en güzel âkıbeti bulmuş, ilerisi için hiçbir ihtiyâcı kalmamış, artık korunmaktan vâreste olmuş ganî addederek hâline, ferdiyetine saplanmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying al-husnā means rejecting the better reward and outcome for those who do good and adopting pessimism that giving and restraint have no benefit.
rows.anchor: “gün günden beterdir, ihsânın korunmanın fâidesi yoktur” diyerek âkıbet hakkında bedbin olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the denier for the hardest end, such as entering the Fire; he cannot overcome the hardship, which overwhelms him.
rows.anchor: girmek gibi en zor ve en güç âkıbete götüren yola müyesser kılacağız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When he falls into the pit, dies, or is destroyed, his wealth cannot rescue him from the grave or ruin and instead increases his punishment and loss.
rows.anchor: Kıyıp veremeyerek topladığı ve onunla zengin olmak, müstağnî kalmak istediği mal onu kabre yuvarlanmaktan, helâk ile esfel-i sâfilîne gitmekten kurtaracak değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teraddā may derive from radā, meaning destruction, or from taraddud, meaning to roll or fall; on the latter analysis its original form is taraddada.
rows.anchor: “Tereddâ (تَرَدَّىٰٓ)” helâk mânasına “redâ”dan yahut yuvarlanmak mânasına “tereddüd”dendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance belongs to God: showing the right path and truth, sending messengers, revealing books, setting signs in the world, and inspiring hearts to distinguish good from evil.
rows.anchor: Felâha çıkaran doğru yolu göstermek, hakk u savâbı beyan etmek, resul göndermek, kitap indirmek, âfâkta edille nasbetmek, enfüste kalblere iyiyi kötüyü ilham eylemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot produce guidance by themselves, though accepting it and walking the path of good is entrusted to their will.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın hidâyeti olmayınca siz kendiliğinizden onu yapamazsınız, ona göre hidâyeti kabul ettirip de hakk u hayr yoluna gitmek de sizin meşiyyetinize mevdû‘bir keyfiyettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This life and the afterlife belong entirely to God, with no competing sovereign; no one can escape by dispensing with His guidance, and defying His will harms only themselves.
rows.anchor: Evvel ü âhir mülk Bizim, hakk-ı tasarruf Bizimdir. Mu‘âraza veya müdahale edecek başka bir mâlik yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning announces a Fire that blazes and grows increasingly fierce.
rows.anchor: bir ateş haber verdim ki alevlendikçe alevlenir, köpürdükçe köpürür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talazzā is a feminine imperfect verb whose original form is tatalaẓẓā; as a past verb with feminine nār, it would be talazzat.
rows.anchor: “Telezzâ (تَلَظَّىٰ)” muzâri‘müennes, aslı “tetelezzâ”dır (تتلظى). Mazi olsa idi -nâr müennes olduğu için- تلظت denilmesi lâzım gelirdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched is the disbeliever, defined as one who denies God's guidance and turns away from the truth.
rows.anchor: “Eşkā”dan murad kâfir olduğu anlatılmak için şununla beyan ve tefsir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner who turns away without denying is wretched but not the most wretched; even if he enters the Fire, he does not remain there.
rows.anchor: Tekzib etmeksizin i‘râz eden fâsık ise en şakī değil şakīdir, o ateşe girerse de yaslanıp kalmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing avoids both disbelief and sin, is kept far from the Fire, never enters it, and passes easily onward to Paradise.
rows.anchor: o ona yaslanıp kalmak şöyle dursun asla girmeyecek, üzerinden kolaylıkla geçip cennete gidecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing gives wealth to purify himself, grow spiritually, and prosper; alternatively, the verb describes giving in order to become purified before God.
rows.anchor: O etkā ki malını verir tezekkî eder temizlenir, tefeyyüz eyler, felah bulur. Yahut “yetezekkâ” hâl olduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He owes no one a compensable favor and does not give as repayment or in expectation of recompense from anyone.
rows.anchor: hiç kimseye medyun ve minnettar değildir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives solely to seek the pleasure of his Most High Lord.
rows.anchor: Ancak Rabb-i a‘lâsının rızâsını aramak için verir, o ciheti gözetir.

rows.speaker: Çokları
rows.claim: Many commentators take the final pronoun to refer to the most God-fearing person, who becomes pleased with his Lord and receives gifts until satisfied.
rows.anchor: Çokları etkāya rücû‘unu zâhir görmüşler, o etkā Rabbinden razı olacak demişlerdir

rows.speaker: İmam Râzî
rows.claim: Razi prefers the pronoun to refer to the Lord because God's pleasure is more eloquent and greater; the servant becomes both pleased and approved, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: İmam Râzî “Rabb”e rücû‘u daha karîb ve daha beliğ olduğunu, çünkü Allah teâlâ’nın rızâsı kulun rızâsından eblağ bulunduğunu söylemiştir

rows.speaker: Hâkim
rows.claim: Al-Hakim grades as sound a report from ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father: Abu Quhafa urges Abu Bakr to free strong slaves, but Abu Bakr says he seeks his own purpose, after which the passage is revealed.
rows.anchor: Hâkim, sahih diye Âmir b. Abdullah b. Zübeyr’den, babasından rivayet etmiş

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir calls the transmitted report authentic and says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr freeing the slaves; a further report specifically associates the verse about owing no one's favor with him.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr der ki: “Âsâr vârid olan sahîhi budur. Demişlerdir ki: Bu, Ebû Bekir âzâd ettiklerini âzâd etmesi sebebiyle onun hakkında nâzil oldu.

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr, who freed six or seven people, including Bilal and Amir ibn Fuhayra, seeking neither repayment nor thanks.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعْمَةٍۢ تُجْزَىٰ kavlinde dedi ki: “Ebû Bekir hakkında nâzil oldu

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a cloak and ten uqiyyas, after which the opening of this surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan tahric etmişlerdir, demiş ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surahs in sequence are al-Duha, al-Sharh, and al-Tin.
rows.anchor: Şimdi bu sûreyi de Duhâ ve İnşirah ve Tîn sûreleri takip edecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duha is the familiar midmorning, when the sun begins to shine and rise and the day is in its youthful phase.
rows.anchor: “Duhâ” diye mâruf olan kuşluk zamanına ki Güneş’in parlayıp yükselmeye başladığı, gündüzün gençliği zamanıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article may be generic, but in this address to the Prophet it more likely points to the singular dawn of truth: the Muhammadan mission beginning to radiate mercy and light to the worlds.
rows.anchor: Hitab Resûlullah’a olmak itibariyle bu ahd mânası râcih olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others connect the oath to the Prophet's face or divine speech; the verse about people gathering at duha also evokes the appointed morning when Moses overcame the magicians.
rows.anchor: vech-i Muhammedîye veya teklîm-i ilâhî zamanına işaret olduğu da söylenmiştir. Nitekim طٰهٰ’da وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًۭى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can describe the settled middle of night, after some time has elapsed, when darkness has reached its depth, covers what it will, and silence falls.
rows.anchor: tam kıvamına gelip durduğu, içindekilerin sükûn bulduğu vakit ki evvelinden bir müddet geçtiği orta demleridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other possibilities are the onset of darkness and covering, the stilling of the wind, or the night drawing to an end; each contrasts or corresponds with duha as grief, joy, or grief's passing.
rows.anchor: Karanlığın çöktüğü, ortalığı örttüğü veya rüzgârın kesildiği veya gecenin tükendiği sıra diye de mülâhaza olunabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajā derives from sujuww, meaning for something to settle and become still; bahr sājī is calm sea, tarf sājī a still eye, and layl sājī a quiet, windless night.
rows.anchor: “Secâ (سَجَىٰ)” “ulüvv” vezninde “sücüvv”dendir. “Sücüvv” mutlaka sükûn, yani bir şey kararını bulup dinmek, sâkin olmak mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same root yields sajiyya for a settled disposition and tasjiya for covering, so the night may be understood as quiet, fully dark and covering, or passing away.
rows.anchor: “Seciyye” dahi sükûn mânasından me’huz olup insanın nefsinde sâkin ve sâbit huy, meleke demektir. “Tesciye” de örtmek mânasına gelir.

rows.speaker: ابن عربي
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says the night has become intensely dark.
rows.anchor: İbn Arabî

rows.speaker: İbn Cübeyr
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr is cited as saying that the night arrives and covers everything.
rows.anchor: Cübeyr’den: اِذَا اَقـْبَلَ فـَغَطَّى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ diye

rows.speaker: İbn Abbâs
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through the Awfi route explains sajā as the night coming on.
rows.anchor: Avfî tarîkiyle İbn Abbas’tan: سَجَا، اَقـْبَلَ diye

rows.speaker: İbn Abbâs
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas explains sajā as the night having gone away.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir ile İbn Ebî Hâtim de ondan سَجَا إِذَا ذَهَبَ diye tahric eylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's basic meaning is stillness and rest, not the force of darkness; the familiar calm, windless night supports this, as does the verse saying night is for rest.
rows.anchor: Cumhûrun beyânına göre asıl sücüvv sükûn demek olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This stillness includes physical and spiritual relief, rest from distress, or the passing of grief as night ends.
rows.anchor: huzur ve istirâhate veya gecenin bitmesi gibi kederin zevâli hengâmına da şâmil olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night can symbolize life's suffering, death's grief, cessation of revelation and knowledge, and spiritual constriction; here the focus is respite during that darkness or the joy that comes when revelation resumes.
rows.anchor: vahyin fütûrunda da bir dinleniş ve tebettül bulunduğunu veya gecenin geçmesi, sabahın başlaması deminde olduğu gibi vahyin fütûru zamanı bitip yeniden başlamasıyla kederin neş’eye tehavvül eylediği zamanı duyurmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duha expresses the bright, youthful joy of life and revealed knowledge, while the settled night signals rest before a promised renewal; this relation fittingly introduces the assurance that the Lord has not abandoned Muhammad.
rows.anchor: gecenin dindiği sükûnu hengâmına kasem olsun ki yâ Muhammed
